meta.title: Full Mock Test 2 — P2
meta.description: ICAI-style pattern (100 marks): 40 MCQs × 1, two case sets × 2, five descriptives × 8. Sit it timed — 3 hours.

questions.q: Under a CONSERVATIVE current-financing policy for a company, which holds?
o: Conservative policy: LT sources fund permanent CA plus part of fluctuating CA — low risk, higher cost
questions.why: Conservative = safety: permanent + part of temporary assets on long-term money; aggressive = the reverse; matching = maturities paired.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — policy-label-to-source matching is definitional AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Long-term financing of part of permanent CA reduces risk, raises cost; match concept.
mem.link: Chapter 1 — Financial Policy and Corporate Strategy

questions.q: Long position hedged with futures; at closing the spot has risen MORE than the futures price. The hedge:
o: Leaves a net gain because the basis (spot − futures) strengthened
questions.why: Perfect hedging requires the spot and futures to move one-for-one; a strengthening basis favours the long spot/short futures hedger (selling the relatively weaker futures) — basis risk is the residue hedging cannot remove.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — hedging converts price risk into basis risk Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Umbrella in one hand, rain in the other — basis is the gap.

questions.q: A project's cash flows are adjusted for risk using certainty equivalents. The discount rate to apply is:
o: Pick ONE: risk-adjusted discount rate OR certainty-equivalent flows
questions.why: Risk loading once: with CE flows (de-risked numerator), discount at the RISK-FREE rate (or without the project premium) — double-adjusting penalises twice.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the double-counting trap is the conceptual point Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Certainty-equivalent: divide cash flows by risk factor; or risk-adjust the rate — never both.

questions.q: Returns with negative skew and excess kurtosis imply the normal distribution:
questions.why: Negative skew = heavier left tail than normal; fat kurtosis = both tails heavier — normal-based risk metrics then understate crash risk; this is the documented case for t-distributions and EVT in stress work.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — normal curve trims the tails — the tails are where you live Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The bell curve has no memory of 2008.

questions.q: Net income Rs 60 crore; capex 60, dep 30, ΔWC 10; debt funds 50% of net capex and WC needs; required return 10%, growth 6%. Equity value via stable-growth FCFE ≈
o: Rs 1,000 crore (equity value, FCFE at g 6%, k 10%)

questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — FCFE leverage-adjustment chain is the valuation flow question AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: FCFE = NI − (1−L)(capex−dep) − (1−L)ΔWC; grow at g.

questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the CML line-equation read is the theory made arithmetic AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: For the MBS investor, falling interest rates create:
o: Contraction risk — principal returns early at par while the bond trades premium, and reinvestment lands at lower rates
questions.why: The homeowner refinances, so the investor's high-coupon asset is returned just when new money earns less (contraction); rising rates extend duration instead — negative convexity is the compact name for this squeeze.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — rates move, timing moves, and the mover holds the option Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The borrower's prepayment is a call option the investor sold for free.

questions.q: Units of a close-ended scheme are:
o: Traded on the stock exchange, with redemption only on buy-back/liquidation as offered — market price may be below NAV
questions.why: Open-ended = continuous liquidity at NAV; close-ended = a fixed corpus whose units change hands at whatever the exchange says — the discount/premium to NAV is the structural feature to quote in any 2-mark answer.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — NAV sets the open-ended price; the crowd sets the close-ended one AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: An open fund promises a door; a closed fund sells a window seat.

questions.q: A call has delta 0.4. The delta-neutral stock holding per call option short is:
o: Hold 0.4 shares per short call (delta hedge)
questions.why: Δ = 0.4 shares per option — short call ⇒ long 0.4 stock keeps net delta zero; re-hedge as Δ moves (gamma).
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — delta-hedge ratios are concept-questions with tiny arithmetic Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Δ shares per option short = delta; position size = Δ per contract.

questions.q: A US subsidiary of an Indian parent operates independently in USD (functional currency). On consolidation the translation differences on its net assets go:
o: Self-sustaining foreign sub: current rate method — translation gain/loss to OCI until disposal
questions.why: Ind AS 21: functional = foreign currency ⇒ current-rate method: all items closing rate, income avg; exchange differences to OCI (CTDR) and recycled on disposal. If integral to parent (temporal): monetary closing, non-monetary historical, differences to P&L.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — functional-currency test driving the method and the destination is the translation exam AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Current rate for self-sufficient sub: equity/retained differences to OCI; temporal for integral: to P&L.
mem.link: Chapter 10 — Foreign Exchange Exposure and Risk Management

questions.q: Translating a foreign subsidiary's equity under Ind AS 21 changes reported reserves; the exposure that actually matters to firm value is:
o: Economic (operating) exposure — sensitivity of cash flows to exchange rates, which need not match any accounting line
questions.why: Translation is an accounting restatement (no cash), economic is the present-value effect of currency on future cash flows — managers hedge economics; the translation line matters for covenants and ratios, which is itself a documented management concern.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the rupee line moves the books; the cash flow moves the value Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The translation loss hits the ledger; the economic loss hits the payroll.

questions.q: For the same duration and rate move, a bond with greater convexity:
o: Loses more on yield rises and gains less on falls
Gains MORE on yield falls than it loses on equal yield rises
Is riskier in both directions identically
questions.why: Convexity is the second-order bonus: price-yield curves bow toward the holder — bigger gains on rallies, smaller losses on sells; portfolios long optionality (callable short ≠) own this; deep discount/MBS cases shift the sign — quote the sign of convexity, never 'curvature' blindly.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — positive convexity is the market paying you for patience Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: A curved ladder is kinder climbing than falling.

questions.q: In a stressed-asset sale/winding-up, the correct payment order is:
o: Workmen' and secured creditors' claims as per the governing insolvency statute, then other claims per the priority ladder of that statute — verify current IBC waterfall order
Promoters last after all creditors, always
questions.why: The IBC (and its amendments and case law have shifted the exact ordering of workmen/taxes vs secured in some tranches) has a statutory waterfall; answer with the statute's ladder and cite that recent amendments have refined it — never recite a 'natural' order.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the statute holds the ladder; case law sometimes re-rungs it Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

questions.q: Monthly burn 40 lakh, cash in bank 4 crore: runway is:
questions.why: Runway = cash ÷ net burn (outflows minus inflows) = 400/40 = 10 months; founders must quote post-burn adjustments (hiring plan) and next-milestone timing against it — mechanical math, judgment caveat.

mem.tip: Cash is the tank; burn is the meter; the milestone is the airport.

questions.q: A bank reports 1-day 99% VaR of ₹50 crore. Correct interpretation:
o: On 99 of 100 days the loss will not exceed 50 crore (1-day horizon, current positions, normal markets)
50 crore is the worst possible loss
questions.why: VaR = the loss threshold exceeded on (1−c) fraction of days under the model's assumptions; it says nothing about the size of the tail it doesn't measure — hence stress tests and expected shortfall supplement it.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — VaR names the cliff edge, not the depth of the fall Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: 99 days of weather, 1 day of free-fall — and VaR won't tell you how far.

questions.q: Which is an INTERNAL credit enhancement for a tranched deal?
o: Subordination plus excess spread within the waterfall
questions.why: Internal = built from the structure itself: subordination, excess spread, reserve accounts funded from deal cash; external = third-party promises (guarantees, LCs, insurance) — the rating of each tranche rides on the internal stack order.

questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — internal is the wall, external is the guard AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The waterfall is its own security blanket; the guarantor is someone else's.

questions.q: Export receivable of $1m in 90 days at ₹83, in 365-day ₹86-forecast terms. Which action manages the transaction exposure?
o: Do nothing and hope for spot gains
Sell the $1m forward for 90-day delivery, locking the rupee value
questions.why: Transaction exposure is the contractual-cash-in-foreign-currency gap within the deal's tenor — hedge the tenor you owe (90 days here); a 365-day hedge overlays speculation on the next year's flows, and future invoicing is a translation-irrelevant decision.

questions.q: Explain two agency conflicts in an Indian promoter-led company and how corporate governance mechanisms (board, regulation, market for corporate control) mitigate them; relate the answer to the wealth-maximisation objective.
questions.ans: Conflict 1: promoter vs minority — tunneling (related-party transactions, encashment of control benefits, preferative placements) extracting private benefits of control; mitigation: audit committee, minority-scheme rules (Reg 19/23 LODR — majority-of-minority approval for related-party schemes), independent directors, disclosure of RPTs. Conflict 2: shareholders vs managers — empire building, perquisite consumption, horizon mismatch (myopic quarterly vs long-term value); mitigation: incentive alignment (ESOPs, performance-linked pay with clawback), board monitoring, threat of takeover in the market for corporate control, debt discipline (free cash flow theory). Link to wealth maximisation: governance mechanisms re-anchor decisions to discounted cash-flow value rather than private benefits or accounting profits, protecting the residual claimants' valuation multiples.
questions.scheme: Each conflict named with Indian manifestation — 3; each mechanism mapped to the conflict — 3; free-cash-flow/market-for-control nuance — 2; wealth-max link — 1; structure — 1.
keyPoints: Ultimate test = present value to shareholders

questions.q: Distinguish risk appetite, tolerance and capacity under ISO-31000/enterprise risk management, and describe the ERM process cycle with an example each for a listed manufacturer.
questions.ans: Capacity = the maximum risk the firm can absorb (capital, covenant, survival bounds — set by resources); Appetite = the amount and type of risk it WANTS to take in pursuit of strategy (board statement); Tolerance = entity-level/operational boundaries near the appetite (e.g., FX VaR ≤ 1.5% of net worth per desk). ERM cycle: (1) establish context (objectives, risk criteria); (2) identification — hazards, exposures (supply disruption, commodity); (3) analysis — likelihood × consequence, modeling (VaR, scenario); (4) evaluation — compare against appetite; (5) treatment — avoid/reduce/share/accept (hedging, insurance, redundancy); (6) monitor & review — KRIs, stress tests; plus communication across. Example: manufacturer accepts ≤25% unhedged oil exposure (tolerance), treats via collars; board reviews via monthly risk dashboard.

questions.q: Compare scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis and Monte-Carlo simulation for a capital project; state what each adds beyond NPV and their key limitation.
questions.ans: Sensitivity: one variable at a time (% change to NPV; tornado ranking) — reveals drivers but ignores interactions and probabilities (each variable moved alone). Scenario: fixed coherent states (worst/base/best with joint shifts + probabilities → EMV and downside focus) — richer but arbitrary, few states captured. Simulation: distributions on inputs (demand, price, cost correlations), thousands of draws → NPV distribution — captures interaction, gives P(NPV<0) and percentiles; limitations: GIGO (garbage input), correlation assumptions, model risk. All three: risk-adjusted view vs single-point NPV at a risk-loaded discount rate; use alongside real-options logic (option to abandon/expand) for full picture.
questions.scheme: Sensitivity mechanics + limitation — 3; scenario features — 3; simulation advantages + drawbacks — 3; 'what they add to NPV' framing — 1.
keyPoints: One-at-a-time vs coherent worlds vs full distributions

questions.q: Define real options and explain the option to WAIT, to ABANDON, and the option to EXPAND, each with one Indian-infrastructure example, noting why Black–Scholes inputs are hard here.
questions.ans: A real option is the right, not obligation, to change the project's cash-flow path when uncertainty resolves; NPV alone ignores that management ADAPTS. Option to wait (deferral): investing now kills the chance to invest at better information — a concession with pricing freedom or ROFR land is an American call on the project; value = NPV + waiting value, so a marginally-positive NPV can still mean 'not yet'. Example: a port terminal awaiting cargo-demand visibility; investing in year 0 forfeits the information value of a year of delay. Option to abandon: after year-3, if demand is low, sell the asset/redeploy the land — a put on liquidation value floor (resaleable plant; contractually returnable assets); it RAISES the project's minimum payoff and can flip a negative static NPV positive. Option to expand: first phase sized small, expansion rights (paid permit, spare land parcel, modular capacity) — a call on the growth NPV; phased capex is the cost of keeping the call alive. BS mapping pain: no traded asset = underlying (use DCF value of PV of inflows), exercise price = capex, variance must be proxied by price/volume history, and 'dividend' (cash flows lost by waiting) is the leak that shrinks the wait value.

questions.q: Describe the three Fama efficiency forms with the test type that would falsify each.
questions.ans: Weak (past prices/technical rules give nothing): falsified by profitable chartist strategies tested by autocorrelation, run tests on returns; semi-strong (public info absorbed): falsified by abnormal returns to public signals — event studies around earnings/stock-splits, dividend announcements; strong (all info incl private): falsified by insider/board trading outperformance, mutual-fund persistence. Practical implications: active management fees vs expected alpha, value of disclosure quality, index-fund logic; anomalies (momentum, January, size) challenge but risk/cost-adjustments defend.
